title: Two October days on the Potomac
intent: Compare published USGS daily mean discharge at Hancock, Point of Rocks and Little Falls on 2024-10-01 and 2025-10-01, while keeping each gauge's limits visible.

scenes.title: Three gauges, one published day
scenes.narration:
The U.S. Geological Survey reports daily mean discharge at three distinct Potomac gauges. On 2024-10-01, the published values were 5,580 ft^3/s at Hancock, 23,600 ft^3/s at Point of Rocks, and 17,300 ft^3/s at Little Falls. The three points mark stable station IDs, not equal drainage areas.

The photograph shows the river area at Whites Ferry as context. It is not a picture of a gauge measurement or of this day.

content.semantics: Published daily mean discharge at three gauges on 2024-10-01.
content.location: Potomac River, Hancock to Little Falls; station-local Eastern time dates.

scenes.title: The same gauges, one year later
scenes.narration: For 2025-10-01, the published daily means were 580 ft^3/s at Hancock, 2,020 ft^3/s at Point of Rocks, and 1,800 ft^3/s at Little Falls. The map keeps the same extent and color scale so each station can be compared across the two dates. These two daily snapshots do not establish a long-term trend or a cause for the differences.

content.semantics: Published daily mean discharge at the same stations on 2025-10-01.
content.relationship: Compare each station with its 2024-10-01 published value using one shared scale.

scenes.title: What the snapshots can tell us
scenes.narration:
These are USGS Approved daily mean discharge records for station-local dates in Eastern time. The records have no additional qualifier, but approval does not make the three catchments interchangeable. Hancock and Point of Rocks have documented regulation or hydroelectric influences; Little Falls has documented diversions and reservoir effects. Different drainage areas and travel time also limit a direct upstream-to-downstream reading.

The two dates support a descriptive station-by-station comparison. They do not measure reach gain or loss, isolate a cause, describe unregulated flow, establish a trend, or assess flood risk.

content.semantics: The meaning and limits of two published station-day summaries.
content.relationship: Return to the same locations while interpreting the comparison.
